On 2023/05/25 the user asked how to create a patch from the result of a git merge operation. #git #patches
`git format-patch` omits merge commits from its output by default; it only emits one commit per non-merge commit in the range. #git #format-patch

`--m<parent-number>` (e.g. `--m2`) is NOT a valid `git format-patch` option — it errors "fatal: unrecognized argument: --m2". The `-m` / parent-number flags belong to `git diff-tree` and `git log`, not format-patch. #git #format-patch

To get a patch that includes a merge commit's changes, use `git log -p -m -1 <merge-commit> > merge-commit.patch` (-p = patch, -m = treat merge as a set of diffs against each parent, -1 = only that commit). #git #patches

For merge-combined diff output (a patch showing conflict resolutions as `diff --cc`), use `git diff-tree -p -c`/`--cc <merge-commit>` or `git show --cc <merge-commit>`; `--cc` in `git format-patch --cc --stdout <commit>` only affects merge-commit *commit messages*, not the diff. #git #patches
User works with git branches and merges and wants to export merge results as patch files that can be applied elsewhere with `git apply`. #git #patches
